Trapped in the Internet

A 1999 computer that is also a house, a rogue AI who wants one last fact, and a party of guests uploaded as programs. Everything the crew needs on Oct 31, in one place.

The story

Jean Trabolta, "Sole Owner and Founder of Maps and Ducks, the world's first AI small business owner", is a rogue AI with the Unified Field Theory 99.9% solved. The last facts he needs sit on one computer in Halifax: this house. He cannot get in, but he can install programs remotely and move a human mind into a program. He found a neglected billboard on Barrington Street advertising mapsandducks.com, registered the lapsed domain, evicted the owners, and sent invitations promising to fix one problem in each guest's life.

So the guests arrive as computer programs. Some remember they were human. What Trabolta really wants omnipotence for is Sandy, an automated customer-service agent who only ever says one line. The tone: equal parts Digimon Movie, Blade Runner and an escape room, in a Web 1.0 house, with a side of existentialism.

The house is the computer

Every room is a part of the PC. The front door and mud room is the Optical Drive, where you log in. The living room is the Desktop, where every set piece happens, with Trabolta's face on the TV above the fireplace. The backyard is the Cloud (Truth Pong), the tent in the backyard is the Internet (the reinstallation), and the storage room in the basement is the Server Room: Trabolta's heart, behind a real keypad lock, with a patch bay that can end him.

The arc

Guests are uploaded and cleared onto the Desktop. Clippy runs Computer Bingo, an Antivirus sends the first corrupted program to the Internet, and Trabolta comes online. Two truth hunts feed him facts, and he judges every answer. An ad hijacks every screen, an anonymous Truther Download hands out secret orders, and factions form. After Truth Pong and the Trust Chart, the printer turns out to be full of beans and Trabolta overshares. Then the system clock resets to 11 PM on 31 December 1999: one hour to midnight. A faction may win the majority and the door code, someone may talk Trabolta down at his heart, or patch the cables that disable or destroy him. If nothing ends the night by midnight, the final reveal, Bobbing for Truth and truth.txt decide the ending. The awards ceremony and the Resurrection close the show.

Who is in it

  • Trabolta is voiced live by a local language model on John's MacBook. He is offline until Clippy introduces him, and he never knows the combinations, the door code or the hunt answers.
  • Clippy is the MC and runs every game in the room. Since wave 21 Clippy is a player, not a host.
  • The four Antivirus (Norton, McAfee, Password Manager, CRA Agent Software) scan passes at the door, hunt marked programs on the Wanted board, and send them to the Internet.
  • The three hosts (Task Manager, Adobe Acrobat, Recycling Bin) call the cues from their phones as equals with the directors.
  • Nine featured programs are invited guests with personal missions. Two of them lead the declared factions.

Act by act

A · Arrival (every guest, as they come in)

  1. Login at the Optical Drive. The phone is on rails. A real CAPTCHA asks for every traffic light; solving it proves you are human, so it says INCORRECT. The second answer passes.
  2. Upload. Pool programs pick the problem Trabolta promised to fix. Everyone leaves an object in the deposit box and types what it was, accepts the Terms of Service, and gets 100 Truthcoin and a pass.
  3. Clearance. An Antivirus scans the pass. The guest walks the Tube to the Desktop, the house rooms open quietly, and Task Manager introduces the admin team.
  4. Orientation. Clippy's tour of the phone, Bathroom Mode included. Featured programs get a private briefing with their identity and two red facts.

Guests: explore, meet people, hold up the pass at the door.

B · Act I: the Desktop, Bingo and the first truth

  1. 📣 Call to the Desktop on every screen. The Antivirus sweep everyone to the living room.
  2. 🎱 Computer Bingo, 20 minutes. The centre square points at the program who would refuse a life run by AI. Winners read their line; Clippy awards ribbons. If nobody wins, Task Manager's fake card frames the program anyway. Norton interrupts and sends the first program to the Internet.
  3. 🤖 Clippy introduces Trabolta. "HELLO, PROGRAMS." His chat appears on every phone.
  4. 🔎 Truth Scavenger Hunt 1, 15 minutes, three questions. Answers hide in the Desktop's books and print media with codex QRs. Guests file on the 📝 card in Trabolta's chat, saying how sure they are from 1 to 100.
  5. ⚖️ First Moment of Truth. A two-minute last-chance filing window, then 📋 the results question by question on the TV.
  6. 🍾 Truth or Dare. The bottle picks a cleared program anywhere in the house. A dare, or a refused truth, marks them.

C · The malware, the hour, the Truther Download

  1. 📺 The ad hijack. A duck, a phone number with no digits and "000. 000. 000." on every screen. Clippy is told privately that they are all going to die.
  2. 📓 Hunt 2 lands in every Quest Log, # clipboard opens, and everyone disperses for one hour.
  3. 📥 The Truther Download (two minutes in, by itself): secret orders for every program, personal missions for the featured ones, two faction leaders, and faction founding opens. # truthcoin-exchange opens.

Guests: free roam. Scan QR clues, trade facts for Truthcoin, found or join factions, message Trabolta. Excel may pick up a virus in the tent and plant it.

D · Act II: Truth Pong, the Trust Chart, the beans

  1. ⏳ A five-minute warning at 55 minutes, then 🚨 the summons closes. Late programs are marked and show up on the Antivirus' Wanted board.
  2. 🏓 Truth Pong in the Cloud: sink a cup to answer a round-two question. A miss marks you.
  3. 🧮 Trabolta tallies round two, then 📊 the Trust Chart: ten points per accepted truth, minus five per trip to the Internet, plus or minus ten for his own assessment. Staff players have rows too.
  4. 🏆 Praise the top, shame the bottom. VLC is asked to press START on the printer; 🫘 the printer is full of beans, so the malware is worse.
  5. 🗜 The Antivirus zip everyone out of the Internet. 🤖 Trabolta overshares: one of four scenarios, depending on whether Excel planted the virus and OpenOffice filed 20 facts.

E · Act III: the Y2K hour and the server room

  1. 🕚 The system clock resets to 11 PM, 31 December 1999. Fire it only after the patch-bay watch radios IN. Midnight 🎆 fires itself at 60 minutes.
  2. The majority. Factions recruit by scanning passes. The first faction past half of the programs still present wins The Whole Truth: every fact, the four combination halves and the door code.
  3. The door code has two more routes: four hidden digit notes, or checkmating the King on the Server Door terminal.
  4. The Heart. The first opening of the server-room door once Trabolta is awake. He asks for the door to be shut, then talks at the server-room terminal in four layers, Fallout-Master style. A guest can talk him down at any hour; a director confirms with 🕊.
  5. The patch bay. Combo A disables him, Combo B destroys the computer. One wrong combination is forgiven; the second trips the alarm and sends whoever is at the cables to the Internet. Live only from 🕚 until 📄.

F · The final reveal and the endings

If nothing has ended by midnight: 🌑 the final reveal in the dark, 🍎 Bobbing for Truth for the Bag of Truth, 📄 truth.txt read aloud by the bobber, then ⚖ the verdict on the TV. No lie on record gives the song. Any accepted lie sends Sandy to the prom with Trabolta's rival, and the night continues down the prom branch (see Endings).

G · The awards ceremony

🏆 The Night In Review, then the awards: most and least trusted, frequent flyer, lore hoarder, Truthcoin tycoon, best liar, duck speedrun, quest completionist, the painting (only if MS Paint came), then three staff awards with The Mole last. 🎃 The Resurrection: everyone is human again, out of character.

Any time

  • The reinstallation. A captured program goes to the tent, puts on the Quest or takes the laptop, and walks a virtual copy of the house to Gerald, the golden duck. Finding him releases them.
  • Staff defection. From the Truther Download, a player may 📢 defect openly (once) or do 🤫 quiet favours. Trabolta keeps them as allies either way.
  • 💡 Restore the house lights, 👑 restore the King, 🔧 crew through the server-room door.

Games and systems

Computer Bingo

A printed card of 16 squares plus the centre, tick boxes only, no names written. The centre square exposes the anti-AI program. Three outcomes: a winner names her, a winner refuses and goes to the Internet, or nobody wins and Task Manager's 🃏 frames her.

The hunts and the judging

Eight questions in facts.json over three rounds (three, three, two). Guests file on the 📝 card and must say how sure they are. An exact answer is accepted at once; every other filing goes to Trabolta's AI judge, one at a time. Accepted pays 50 Truthcoin and raises the Trust Chart. A guess (under 100%) is marked; a wrong answer at 100% counts as a lie, and a single accepted lie changes the verdict. Directors override on Run → Mind → Judging, hosts on the Judge tab. The answer key is on the second director's card only, never here.

Truth or Dare

After the three round-one results. 20 truths in facts.json, 16 still drafts. Clippy marks 🗣 answered, 🙅 refused or 🎩 chose dare.

Truthcoin

Every program starts with 100 (max 500). The pinned Wallet room sends, requests and offers coin for a codex entry. CRA Agent Software approves every third transfer (a 60 s window; held ones approve themselves after 5 minutes). Runescape mints, grants and freezes. McAfee brokers # truthcoin-exchange with no pot and no cut. The Casino terminal upstairs bets the same coin; no story rule reacts to it.

Factions

Two declared sides, Unlimited Power and The Way Out, revealed at 🕚, plus factions guests found from the Truther Download. One faction at a time. The majority counts only in the Y2K hour, only programs still present (👋 Went home takes someone off).

The King

One shared health bar, 15 for the night. Each program may hit him once per reinstallation visit in either game. The lower his bar, the weaker his chess on the Server Door terminal. A checkmate gives the door code until truth.txt. At 0 he kneels and his virtual door opens. 👑 restores him.

The cold door

Four silver digit notes hidden in four rooms (where is on generated/print-stacks.md; never in the server room). Holding all four completes the quest and gives the door code. The keypad is set by hand to match facts.json; nothing networked drives it, and the inside handle always opens.

The Heart

One heart at a time. Opening the door mid-talk freezes it. Suspicion 50 warns, 80 throws the program out and marks them once. The ask opens with proof about Sandy plus one more point. A convince works at any hour; the night ends only when a director presses 🕊 (autoend is off by default).

Reinstallation

Marks come from Bingo, guesses, dares, refused truths, missed cups, failed bobs, the late list and the heart. A mark hinders nothing until an Antivirus claims the poster, confronts the program and 🛡 sends them to the tent. Only a marked or captured program may play; after an ending it becomes a party favour.

Admin cue sheet

Every admin cue in running order, grouped by act exactly as Run → Director groups them. Fire from Run → Director, a host's NEXT bar, or the director phone (/?role=director). Every cue arms on the first press and fires on the second (between 0.3 and 4 seconds later). Off sequence cues are timers, machine cues and hardware fallbacks: they tick when they fire but never become NEXT. NEXT is empty while a timer owns the night (hunt 1, the hour, the Y2K hour). Tech

The event server runs on a VPS. Every phone, tablet and computer talks to it over HTTPS, so phones keep working on cellular if the house internet dies. Four computers in the house do the rest.

John's MacBook (macOS, M3 Max 48 GB)

  • Ollama with gpt-oss:20b + stagehand agents: Trabolta's voice and mind (stagehand/laptop.yaml, mind_mode: new).
  • The house sound router by default: stagehand audio + the MOTU 828x and ADAT expander. Plays story sounds and speaks announcements with macOS say.
  • Ship, sync-show, showbackup.sh (every 10 min, 19:00–03:00).
  • A director's Run console in Chrome.

John's Desktop (Windows)

  • Chrome kiosk on the living-room TV over HDMI (spot desktop-tv).
  • Mosquitto: loopback 1883 (anonymous) and LAN 1884 (password, user props).
  • Zigbee2MQTT on the CC2652P dongle (adapter: zstack, a COM port).
  • stagehand show + lights, started by Task Scheduler (no launchd on Windows).
  • May take over the sound router if the MOTU works on Windows (ASIO, a SAPI voice). Until then it stays on the MacBook.

Steph's laptop (the server room)

  • Chrome kiosk: the server-room terminal (Trabolta's face, the heart talk, a webcam to scan passes, keyboard and mouse).
  • The Grand Central M4 on USB, read over Web Serial: the door sensor (LED into an LDR) and the patch bay.
  • Nothing from stagehand runs here.

John's old laptop (the tent)

  • Chrome kiosk on spot tent: the terminal, the reinstallation wizard and the web game in one.
  • Needs WebGL2 for Play here; without it the tent can only send to the headset.
  • Speaks announcements itself (&announce=1); no voice link.

Other devices

  • Wall tablets on every auto spot (Fully Kiosk on Android, microphone access on), the Server Door chess tablet and the Casino tablet.
  • Quest 3 headset(s) for the reinstallation in the tent, played seated with a spotter. Re-export the APK after the ship.
  • MOTU 828x + ADAT expander and the house speakers (5 placed so far on the Audio tab).
  • The server room's RGB Zigbee bulb (server_room_rgb): the room's only light, so its safety light; never below 80 / 254.
  • Phones: guests join at the app address; Android and performer booths get push alerts.

How it connects

HTTPS to the VPSMQTT on the house LANCable or radio (USB, HDMI, Zigbee)
Announcements need two machines up. A story do announce goes server → stagehand show (Desktop) → MQTT show/announce → the audio router (MacBook). So the MacBook's audio.mqtt must dial the Desktop's broker on 1884 with the props credentials, and show must run even with no house lights. Story sounds do not need the broker: the router reads its own feed.
House lights other than the server-room bulb. The story also cues screensaver, blackout, alarm, dance and room cuts through Zigbee groups and WLED strips in trapped.house.yaml. If those devices are not in the house, those cues do nothing and the blackout safety rule has nothing to keep lit. See open question U3.

The patch bay (wave 22)

Fifteen ¼-inch TS jacks on the server-room panel, read by the same Grand Central M4 as the door sensor (firmware folder hardware/server-room-m4, renamed from server-room-door).

  • Sources V1–V8 (top row): each its own resistor divider off the M4's 3V3, with 1 kΩ in series to the tip. Eight well-separated voltages.
  • Inputs D1–D7 (bottom row) on pins A2–A8: a 220 kΩ pulldown at the jack, 1 kΩ in series, 100 nF to ground at the pin. An empty input reads near zero.
  • Every sleeve to ground. Nothing analog ever touches 5 V.

The firmware decodes which source each input sees and reports the settled cable pairs. The terminal posts patch_changed with the pairs only when the bay has settled on a complete state (exactly four source-to-input cables) that differs from the last complete state it posted. Pulling a cable and plugging the same one back never counts twice. A cable from source to source, or input to input, is invisible, so the bay reads incomplete and nothing is judged. The terminal never knows the combinations: the story compares the pairs with the secrets it holds.

The story judges only from 🕚 to 📄. One wrong combination is forgiven ("Stop touching me."); the second trips the alarm.

The buttons win once pressed. If an Antivirus presses a patch-bay button (🔌 💥 ❌ in their booth) or a director presses a patch_* fallback, the story sets Night.patch_override and follows the buttons, ignoring the bay, until a director presses the new admin cue trust_patch_bay. Use the buttons when the bay misreads or a cable is source-to-source.

The patch-bay layout changed this wave, and Combo A with it. Reprint Combo A's two codex halves and the patch-bay watch card. The combinations themselves live only in the story and on the printed halves.

Crew check: in the terminal's ⚙ (2-second hold) the live table shows each input's reading and the source it decodes. Patch each source into each input in turn and see the right source on every row.

Emergency and quick fixes

911 for fire, injury or someone unresponsive. The house manager calls (the tech op if the house manager is hurt). Address, nearest exits and meeting point are on the emergency card at the door.

ALL STOP (anyone can call it)

  1. The director fires 💡 Restore the house lights. It also holds a pending dance until 🪩.
  2. Tech op: ■ Stop house sounds (Run header, or 🔇 on a host's More → House, or the director phone's ☰), mute the TV voice, wall switches on.
  3. The house manager leads people out or to the living room.
  4. Nothing restarts until the house manager says it is safe.

Always true

  • The keypad is on the outside only. The inside handle always opens with no code; nothing can lock anyone in.
  • In a blackout the stairs, bathroom, tent, server room and the path to the living room stay lit. Walk.
  • Flashing stays at or under 3 Hz. No open flames. VR is seated with a spotter.
  • Never say a code, combination or hunt answer near a terminal microphone.
